mainTopic: The source that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת, where only שמואל's וחי בהם survives, and the משנה and גמרא on how קרבנות, יום הכפורים and תשובה bring atonement.
overview: This amud joins the sugya in the middle. רבי עקיבא is finishing his proof that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת. רבי אלעזר, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, רבי יונתן בן יוסף and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא each bring another proof. שמואל then gives וחי בהם: live by the מצוות, and do not die by them. רבא shows that every other proof covers only a certain danger, not a ספק. Only שמואל's proof has no refutation, and it is praised as 'one sharp pepper.' A new משנה follows. It teaches that קרבנות, מיתה, יום הכפורים and תשובה each bring atonement in different ways, and that sins against another person need appeasement. The גמרא then reads the משנה closely. It explains why אשם תלוי is left out, and it shows the משנה can fit רבי's view that יום הכפורים atones even without תשובה. Last, רב יהודה explains which לא תעשה תשובה alone atones for. A contradicting ברייתא is then brought, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's proof from the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא finishes his proof. A כהן is taken even from the altar to save a life, and the עבודה overrides שבת. So by קל וחומר, פיקוח נפש overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But to save a life, we take him even off My altar. This כהן's testimony might help or might not help. He is still pulled away from the עבודה, and the עבודה itself overrides שבת. So by קל וחומר, saving a life overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining רבי עקיבא's proof in the middle. He shows that saving a life is more important than the עבודה in the בית המקדש, and the עבודה is more important than שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps of the logic are: עבודה pushes aside שבת, and the mere chance of saving a life pushes aside עבודה. So saving a life must certainly push aside שבת. The phrase 'maybe his words have substance, maybe not' matters because it shows we act even when the life-saving is only a possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lesser case to a greater case
Saving a life that is in danger

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'off My altar' is not about saving the כהן himself. The כהן is taken away from his service so that he can testify and save someone else who is on trial.

phrases.english: But to save a life —
phrases.notes: Compare the first half: to put someone to death, we take him 'from' the altar, but not off the top of it.

phrases.english: even from on top of My altar.
phrases.notes: Even in the middle of the service.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה זֶה, שֶׁסָּפֵק יֵשׁ מַמָּשׁ בִּדְבָרָיו
phrases.english: And just as this one, where it is uncertain whether his words have substance
phrases.notes: His testimony might save the defendant.

phrases.english: or whether his words have no substance,
phrases.notes: Or it might not help at all.

phrases.english: and the Temple service overrides Shabbat —
all the more so for saving a life,
that it overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes רבי עקיבא's derivation, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A possible chance of saving a life overrides עבודה, which overrides שבת. Therefore פיקוח נפש overrides שבת.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's proof from circumcision
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר argues that if מילה, which concerns one limb, overrides שבת, then saving the whole body certainly does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר answered and said: מילה involves only one of the 248 limbs of a person, and it overrides שבת. So by קל וחומר, saving a person's whole body overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage gives a different קל וחומר to prove the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה fixes one limb and still pushes aside שבת. A whole person is much more than one limb. So saving the whole person should certainly push aside שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar answered and said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.english: Just as circumcision, which is one
of the 248 limbs in a person,
overrides Shabbat —
all the more so for his entire body,
that it overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This offers another קל וחומר in place of רבי עקיבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since מילה, which involves one limb, overrides שבת, saving the whole body certainly overrides שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה learns from the word 'but'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns from the limiting word אך that keeping שבת has exceptions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: the פסוק says 'Keep My שבתות.' I might think this applies in every case. So the פסוק adds 'but' (אך), which makes a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the proofs move from logical arguments to פסוקים. This sage reads the small word אך as limiting the command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אך means 'but' or 'only,' and it signals an exception. It teaches that some situations do not call for keeping שבת. Saving a life is one of those situations.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
"Keep My Shabbatot" (Exodus 31:13),
one might think it applies in all cases —
therefore the verse says "but," which distinguishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֶת שַׁבְּתוֹתַי תִּשְׁמוֹרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new source, a פסוק instead of a קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word אך limits the obligation to keep שבת, which allows breaking it to save a life.

steps.title: רבי יונתן בן יוסף: שבת is given to you
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן בן יוסף learns from 'it is holy to you' that שבת is placed in our hands, and we are not handed over to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן בן יוסף says: the פסוק says 'For it is holy to you.' This means שבת is given into your hands, and you are not given into its hands.
steps.whatsHappening: Another sage gives a different פסוק for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לכם, 'to you,' is read as meaning that שבת was given for the benefit of people. So a person does not have to die for the sake of שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef says:
"For it is holy to you" (Exodus 31:14),
it is given into your hands,
and you are not given into its hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר: כִּי קוֹדֶשׁ הִיא לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another separate source from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת exists for people, so a person is not required to die for it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: break one שבת to keep many
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא learns from 'the Children of Israel shall keep Shabbat' that we break one שבת so the person can keep many more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: the פסוק says 'בני ישראל shall keep שבת.' The תורה said: break one שבת for him, so that he will keep many שבתות.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth source is given. This one is based on the goal of keeping שבת in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is about the future. If the person survives, he will keep many more שבתות. So breaking one שבת now actually serves the purpose of keeping שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
"And the Children of Israel shall keep Shabbat" (Exodus 31:16),

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: חַלֵּל עָלָיו שַׁבָּת אַחַת
phrases.english: the Torah said: desecrate one Shabbat for him
so that he will keep many Shabbatot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר: וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another separate source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking one שבת is allowed so that the person will keep many future שבתות.

steps.title: שמואל's proof: 'and live by them'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says his source is better than all the others: וחי בהם, 'live by them' and not die by them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if I had been there, I would have said that my source is better than theirs. The פסוק says 'and live by them,' which means a person should not die because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא, שמואל, says that he would have offered a stronger source than all the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: וחי בהם is a general rule about all the מצוות. They are given so that a person lives by them, not so that he dies by keeping them. This one פסוק covers every case, including a case where the danger is uncertain.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall live by them (Leviticus 18:5)

steps.whyThisMatters: וחי בהם becomes the main and best-known source for פיקוח נפש throughout the Torah.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If I had been there,
I would have said that mine is better than theirs:
"And he shall live by them" —
and not that he should die by them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a later source that claims to be better than all the earlier ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of וחי בהם, a person should not die for the sake of a מצוה, so פיקוח נפש overrides שבת.

steps.title: רבא: only שמואל's proof cannot be refuted
steps.stepSummary: רבא judges all the proofs. Every one of them can be refuted except שמואל's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: every one of them has a refutation, except for שמואל's, which has no refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his overall judgment. This line sets up what comes next, where the גמרא goes through the proofs one at a time and shows how each one fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not argue with the rule itself. Everyone agrees that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת. He is checking which source actually proves it in every case.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not rejecting the halacha. He is only rejecting the earlier sources as proof for every case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: לְכוּלְּהוּ אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: All of them have a refutation,
except for Shmuel's, which has no refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְכוּלְּהוּ אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This judges all of the earlier proofs together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only שמואל's source, וחי בהם, has no refutation.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's break-in proof refuted with רבא's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל's proof from מחתרת can be pushed off using רבא's explanation. The burglar is presumed to be ready to kill, so killing him is self-defense against a danger treated as certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל's proof can perhaps be explained the way רבא explains it. רבא said: what is the reason for the law of מחתרת? There is a חזקה that a person does not hold back when someone takes his money. The thief knows the owner will stand up against him. He tells himself: if he stands against me, I will kill him. And the Torah said: if someone comes to kill you, get up early and kill him first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now applies רבא's general claim to the first proof, which is רבי ישמעאל's proof from the burglar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל wanted to show that even an uncertain danger to life justifies breaking rules. רבא's חזקה changes how we see the case. The burglar is presumed to have decided to kill, so it is not really a case of doubt. It is treated as a case of certain danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking in by tunneling; the burglar case
Get up early to kill him; strike first

phrases.english: That of Rabbi Yishmael — perhaps it is like Rava's view.
phrases.notes: The proof was given earlier in the sugya.

phrases.english: For Rava said: What is the reason for the break-in law?

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָקָה, אֵין אָדָם מַעֲמִיד עַצְמוֹ עַל מָמוֹנוֹ.
phrases.english: It is a presumption: a person does not hold himself back regarding his money.
And this thief knows that he will stand up against him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר אִי קָאֵי לְאַפַּאי — קָטֵילְנָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and he said: if he stands against me, I will kill him,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה: בָּא לְהׇרְגְּךָ — הַשְׁכֵּם לְהׇרְגוֹ.
phrases.english: and the Torah said: if one comes to kill you, rise early to kill him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first specific example of רבא's general claim.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Because of the חזקה, the burglar case counts as a certain threat to life, not a doubtful one.

steps.title: Certain danger is proven, but what about uncertain danger?
steps.stepSummary: The refutation ends: מחתרת teaches only about danger that is certain, so where do we learn that we break שבת when the danger is only a ספק?
steps.simpleTranslation: So we have found a source for a case where the danger is certain. From where do we learn the case where the danger is uncertain?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question finishes the refutation of רבי ישמעאל. His case does not prove the rule for a ספק, an uncertain danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha is that we break שבת even when we are not sure a life is in danger. The burglar case only proves the rule for certain danger, so it does not prove the whole rule.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל's מחתרת proof falls because the burglar case is treated as a certain danger. We still need a source for a ספק פיקוח נפש.

phrases.english: We have found a source for a certain case; from where do we know an uncertain case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This states the flaw that רבא's reasoning exposed in the previous step.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof covers only certain danger, while the halacha also includes uncertain danger.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's proof is pushed off using אביי
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's proof (taking a כהן away from the מזבח to testify and save a life) can be refuted. Following אביי, two rabbis first check that the testimony has real substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא's proof can also be pushed off. Maybe it follows אביי, who said: we send a pair of rabbis with him to find out whether his words have real substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now refutes רבי עקיבא's proof, the same way it refuted רבי ישמעאל's proof in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learned that saving a life pushes aside עבודה, because a כהן is taken from the מזבח to testify for an accused man. אביי says two rabbis first check that this testimony is real before the כהן is pulled away. So the case only shows that we interrupt the עבודה when the rescue is certain.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; introduces a possible alternate reading that weakens a proof
A pair of rabbis (sent to check the claim)
Real substance in his words (his testimony is meaningful)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva's proof also —
phrases.notes: Refers to his proof from 'מעם מזבחי תקחנו למות', where a כהן is taken from the altar to testify.

phrases.english: perhaps it is like Abaye's view.
For Abaye said:
we send with him a pair of rabbis
phrases.notes: They accompany the כהן who claims to have testimony.

phrases.english: to know whether there is substance to his words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's refutation pattern from steps 8 and 9 to the next proof, רבי עקיבא's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof's power to cover a ספק. It does not reject the rule that saving a life pushes aside עבודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The testimony is checked first, so the rescue is certain (ודאי), not doubtful.

steps.title: So we still have no source for doubtful danger
steps.stepSummary: After the refutation, רבי עקיבא's proof teaches only about certain danger. Where do we learn the rule for a ספק?
steps.simpleTranslation: So we have found a source for certain danger. For doubtful danger, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the refutation of רבי עקיבא with the same question it asked in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof still works for ודאי. But the real question of the sugya is a ספק נפשות, and this proof no longer reaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain (a danger or rescue that is definite)
From where do we know it? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: So we have found certain cases;
doubt, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the refutation begun in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's proof as a source for ספק פיקוח נפש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A proof that only covers certain rescue cannot be the source for breaking a rule when the danger is uncertain.

steps.title: All proofs fall except שמואל's
steps.stepSummary: Every proof covers only ודאי, not ספק. Only שמואל's source, וחי בהם, has no refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for all of them, we have found certain cases; doubt, from where do we know it? But שמואל's proof certainly has no refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up רבא's review: every proof is limited to certain danger, and only שמואל's survives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: וחי בהם means you should live by the מצוות and not die because of them. That covers even a possible risk to life. So it is the only source that reaches a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them (all the earlier proofs)

steps.whatToRemember: Every proof except שמואל's covers only certain danger. Only וחי בהם teaches that we break שבת even for a ספק נפשות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why, in practice, we break שבת even when it is unclear whether a life is truly in danger.

phrases.english: And for all of them, we have found certain cases;
doubt, from where do we know it?
But Shmuel's proof certainly has no refutation.
phrases.notes: Here the word וַדַּאי means 'certainly'. It is not the legal term for certain danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ אַשְׁכְּחַן וַדַּאי, סָפֵק מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the refutation from one proof to all of them, and confirms רבא's verdict from step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only וחי בהם proves that we break שבת for a ספק of danger to life.

steps.title: One sharp pepper beats a basket of squash
steps.stepSummary: רבינא (or רב נחמן בר יצחק) praises שמואל's proof. One sharp proof is better than a whole basket of weak ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said, and some say it was רב נחמן בר יצחק: one sharp pepper is better than a basket full of squash.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion with a saying that praises שמואל's short but powerful source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The many earlier proofs are like a big basket of bland squash. Each one falls short. שמואל's single פסוק is like one spicy pepper: small, but it does the whole job.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another possible author of the saying)

phrases.english: Ravina said,
and some say it was Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
better is one sharp pepper
than a basket full of squash.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָבָא חֲדָא פִּלְפַּלְתָּא חֲרִיפָא מִמְּלָא צַנָּא דְקָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A closing comment of praise on the conclusion reached in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The quality of a proof matters more than the number of proofs.

steps.title: Offerings atone; מיתה and יום הכפורים atone with תשובה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. A חטאת and an אשם ודאי atone. מיתה and יום הכפורים atone only together with תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A חטאת and an אשם ודאי atone. Death and יום הכפורים atone together with תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists what brings atonement for sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבנות atone for the specific sins they are brought for. מיתה and יום הכפורים are stronger, but they need the person's תשובה to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
A definite guilt-offering (for example, for theft or מעילה)

steps.confusionAlert: אשם ודאי does not mean the offering 'certainly atones'. It is the name of a type of offering: an אשם brought for a definite sin, as opposed to an אשם תלוי, which is brought when you are unsure whether you sinned.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A sin-offering and a definite guilt-offering atone.
Death and Yom Kippur —
atone together with repentance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, atonement, after the end of the פיקוח נפש sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings atone. מיתה and יום הכפורים atone only with תשובה.

steps.title: How far repentance alone reaches
steps.stepSummary: תשובה alone atones for light sins (a missed עשה or a לא תעשה). For severe sins, it holds off the punishment until יום הכפורים atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: תשובה atones for light sins: for an עשה and for a לא תעשה. For severe sins it holds things in suspense until יום הכפורים comes and atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what תשובה can do by itself, without יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For light sins, תשובה alone is enough. For severe sins, תשובה is still needed, but it only holds the punishment back. Full atonement comes with יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: Repentance atones for light sins:
for a positive commandment and for a negative commandment.
And for the severe ones, it holds things in suspense
until Yom Kippur comes and atones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list by explaining the reach of תשובה alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה atones fully for light sins, and holds off the punishment for severe sins until יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Planning to sin and rely on atonement does not work
steps.stepSummary: Someone who plans to sin and then repent is not given the chance to repent. Someone who sins while relying on יום הכפורים gets no atonement from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says, 'I will sin and repent, I will sin and repent,' is not given the opportunity to do תשובה. One who says, 'I will sin and יום הכפורים will atone,' יום הכפורים does not atone for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit: the tools of atonement do not work for someone who uses them as a plan to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תשובה and יום הכפורים are gifts for someone who truly regrets a sin. A person who builds them into his plan to sin loses their help.

keyTerms.meaning: I will sin and then repent
He is not given the opportunity (Heaven does not help him)

phrases.english: One who says: I will sin and repent, I will sin and repent —
he is not given the opportunity to repent.
One who says: I will sin and Yom Kippur will atone —
Yom Kippur does not atone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the atonement rules just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relying on תשובה or יום הכפורים in order to sin cancels their help.

steps.title: Sins against others need appeasement
steps.stepSummary: יום הכפורים atones for sins between a person and הקב״ה. For sins against another person, it does not atone until the victim is appeased.
steps.simpleTranslation: For sins between a person and God, יום הכפורים atones. For sins between a person and his fellow, יום הכפורים does not atone until he appeases his fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets one more limit on יום הכפורים: it does not cover sins against people by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These sins still count as sins, and יום הכפורים can atone for them. It just has an extra condition: first make peace with the person you hurt.

keyTerms.meaning: Between a person and his fellow
That he appeases (wins over the person he hurt)

steps.whatToRemember: יום הכפורים does not wipe away harm done to another person until you appease him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of asking others for forgiveness before יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: Sins between a person and God —
Yom Kippur atones;
sins between a person and his fellow —
Yom Kippur does not atone
until he appeases his fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבֵּין אָדָם לַמָּקוֹם יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another condition on when יום הכפורים atones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sins against another person need appeasement before יום הכפורים atones for them.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's verse for this rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reads 'מכל חטאתיכם לפני ה׳ תטהרו' as teaching that יום הכפורים cleanses only the sins that are 'before ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה expounded: 'From all your sins before ה׳ you shall be cleansed.' Sins between a person and God, יום הכפורים atones. Sins between a person and his fellow, יום הכפורים does not atone until he appeases his fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the משנה, a תנא brings a פסוק as the source for the rule just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'before ה׳' as describing which sins are meant: the sins that are only between you and הקב״ה. Sins that also involve another person need that person's forgiveness too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya expounded:
'From all your sins before the Lord you shall be cleansed' (Vayikra 16:30).
Sins between a person and God —
Yom Kippur atones.
Sins between a person and his fellow —
Yom Kippur does not atone
until he appeases his fellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the rule in step 17. The משנה repeats that rule here on purpose, as the meaning of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that יום הכפורים does not atone for sins against another person without appeasement
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'מכל חטאתיכם לפני ה׳ תטהרו', where the words 'לפני ה׳' are read as limiting which sins are cleansed

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: ה׳ purifies ישראל like a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא closes the משנה with praise. ישראל are purified before their Father in Heaven, who purifies them the way a מקוה purifies the impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: Fortunate are you, ישראל! Before whom are you purified, and who purifies you? Your Father in Heaven, as it says: 'I will sprinkle pure water upon you and you shall be purified.' And it says: 'The מקוה of ישראל is ה׳.' Just as a מקוה purifies the impure, so too הקב״ה purifies ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי עקיבא's words of praise about how הקב״ה Himself purifies ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses two פסוקים. One describes ה׳ sprinkling pure water on us. The other uses a wordplay: מקוה means both 'hope' and 'ritual bath'. Just as a מקוה makes a person pure, הקב״ה makes ישראל pure on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends on a note of comfort: on יום הכפורים, הקב״ה Himself purifies ישראל, like a מקוה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
Fortunate are you, Israel!
Before whom are you purified,
and who purifies you?
Your Father in Heaven,
as it says: 'I will sprinkle pure water upon you and you shall be purified' (Yechezkel 36:25),
and it says: 'The mikveh of Israel is ה׳' (Yirmiyahu 17:13).
phrases.notes: In the פסוק, מקוה simply means 'hope'. רבי עקיבא reads it as 'ritual bath'.

phrases.english: Just as a mikveh purifies the impure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְטַהֵר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: so too the Holy One, Blessed be He, purifies Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with praise built on the theme 'לפני ה׳ תטהרו' from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב״ה Himself purifies ישראל of their sins, the way a מקוה purifies the impure.

steps.title: Only the definite guilt-offering is listed as atoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's wording that אשם ודאי atones, but אשם תלוי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A definite guilt-offering, yes, it atones. An uncertain guilt-offering, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by reading the משנה closely. It notices that the משנה mentions only the 'definite' guilt-offering. This is a setup for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה it said that חטאת and אשם ודאי atone. By naming only the 'definite' אשם, the משנה seems to leave out the אשם תלוי, the offering a person brings when he is unsure whether he sinned. The גמרא draws out this hidden implication so it can question it.

keyTerms.meaning: A definite guilt-offering, brought for a sin the person knows he did
An uncertain or 'suspended' guilt-offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned
Yes / no. This is the classic formula for drawing an inference from wording

phrases.english: Gemara:
A definite guilt-offering — yes (it atones)
An uncertain guilt-offering — no
phrases.notes: We learn this because the משנה doesn't mention it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָשָׁם וַדַּאי — אִין, אָשָׁם תָּלוּי — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the end of the משנה (Step 19) to the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's earlier line about offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication, the משנה excludes אשם תלוי from the offerings that atone.

steps.title: But the Torah says the uncertain offering atones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference: the Torah explicitly uses the word 'atonement' for אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't atonement written about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the inference from Step 20. The Torah itself says that אשם תלוי brings כפרה, so how can the משנה exclude it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about אשם תלוי (ויקרא ה) says 'וכפר עליו הכהן', meaning 'the כהן shall atone for him'. So it looks like a verse contradicts the משנה's implied exclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it so that...?' This introduces a challenge
It is written about it, in the Torah

phrases.english: But isn't atonement written regarding it?
phrases.notes: The verse says 'וכפר עליו' about אשם תלוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that אשם תלוי does not atone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse explicitly attributes כפרה to אשם תלוי, so excluding it contradicts the Torah.

steps.title: The uncertain offering gives only partial atonement
steps.stepSummary: The other offerings bring complete atonement. אשם תלוי brings only incomplete atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those offerings bring full atonement. An uncertain guilt-offering does not bring full atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Yes, אשם תלוי atones, but only partially. The משנה listed only the offerings that bring full atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשם תלוי protects the person from punishment for now. If he later finds out that he really sinned, he must still bring a חטאת. So the Torah's word 'atonement' is true, and the משנה's exclusion is also true, because the משנה is talking about complete atonement.

phrases.english: Those atone with a complete atonement
an uncertain guilt-offering does not atone
with a complete atonement
phrases.notes: It only shields the person until he learns whether he sinned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah says אשם תלוי atones, it should be listed with the others.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only offerings that bring complete atonement. אשם תלוי brings only temporary atonement.

steps.title: The uncertain offering can be replaced by something else
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: nothing can replace the atonement of חטאת and אשם ודאי, but something else can replace the atonement of אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: for those offerings, nothing else can bring their atonement. For the uncertain guilt-offering, something else can bring its atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to explain why the משנה left out אשם תלוי. This answer is about whether the offering can be replaced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת and אשם ודאי are the only way to get their atonement. Nothing substitutes for them. The atonement of אשם תלוי can come from another source, so the משנה did not list it. The next step proves what that other source is.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively. This introduces a second answer

phrases.english: Alternatively
for those, nothing else achieves their atonement
for an uncertain guilt-offering, something else achieves its atonement

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: הָנָךְ אֵין אַחֵר מְכַפֵּר כַּפָּרָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the קשיא of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by whether the offering can be replaced
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אשם תלוי should be listed, since it atones.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only offerings whose atonement nothing else can provide.

steps.title: Proof: יום הכפורים exempts the uncertain offering
steps.stepSummary: A משנה proves the point. After יום הכפורים, people who owe חטאות and definite אשמות still must bring them, but people who owe אשמות תלויין are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: people obligated to bring sin-offerings and definite guilt-offerings, over whom יום הכפורים passed, are still obligated. Those obligated in uncertain guilt-offerings are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support the second answer. It shows that the 'something else' is יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once יום הכפורים passes, the obligation to bring an אשם תלוי falls away, because the day itself atoned. A חטאת or אשם ודאי, however, is still owed. This proves that only the atonement of אשם תלוי can be replaced.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: אשם תלוי gives only temporary atonement, and יום הכפורים can replace it. חטאת and אשם ודאי give full atonement and cannot be replaced.

phrases.english: as we learned in a mishna
those obligated to bring sin-offerings and definite guilt-offerings
over whom Yom Kippur passed — are still obligated
uncertain guilt-offerings — are exempt
phrases.notes: יום הכפורים took the place of their atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second answer (Step 23) by naming the substitute.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that something else can replace the atonement of אשם תלוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (כריתות) ruling that יום הכפורים exempts people who owe אשמות תלויין

steps.title: Death and יום הכפורים atone only with repentance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and infers that without תשובה, death and יום הכפורים do not atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Death and יום הכפורים atone together with repentance. With repentance, yes. On their own, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and reads it closely. This sets up a possible clash with רבי in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עם התשובה' suggest that תשובה is a required ingredient. So the inference is that יום הכפורים alone, without תשובה, gives no atonement.

phrases.english: Death and Yom Kippur
atone together with repentance
With repentance — yes
By themselves — no

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיתָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפְּרִין עִם הַתְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication, יום הכפורים without תשובה does not atone.

steps.title: Does this contradict רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה disagrees with רבי, who holds that יום הכפורים atones even without תשובה, except for three severe sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה does not follow רבי? A ברייתא teaches that רבי says: for all sins in the Torah, whether a person repented or not, יום הכפורים atones. The exceptions are one who throws off the yoke, one who twists the Torah's meaning, and one who breaks the covenant of מילה. For these, if he repented, יום הכפורים atones, and if he did not repent, it does not atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. The inference from Step 25 seems to go against רבי's view in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, יום הכפורים works even without תשובה for almost every sin. תשובה is needed only for three rebellious sins. The משנה seems to require תשובה always, so it appears not to follow רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? This introduces a tentative suggestion
One who throws off the yoke of Heaven
One who interprets the Torah falsely or brazenly
One who breaks the covenant of מילה

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'נימא' makes this a tentative suggestion, not a final conclusion. The next step rejects it.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is not in accordance with Rabbi?
As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi says
for all transgressions in the Torah
whether he repented
or did not repent
Yom Kippur atones
except for one who throws off the yoke
and one who interprets the Torah falsely
and one who breaks the covenant of the flesh
for whom, if he repented,
Yom Kippur atones
and if he did not repent
Yom Kippur does not atone

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the inference of Step 25 against רבי's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implied rule that יום הכפורים requires תשובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי holds that יום הכפורים atones without תשובה for most sins, so the משנה would contradict רבי.

steps.title: Even רבי agrees: repentance needs יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can follow רבי. Its point is that תשובה needs יום הכפורים, not that יום הכפורים needs תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי. Repentance needs יום הכפורים, but יום הכפורים does not need repentance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that the משנה disagrees with רבי. It reads 'with תשובה' in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not mean that תשובה is required for יום הכפורים to work. It means that תשובה alone is not enough for severe sins: it must wait for יום הכפורים to finish the atonement. So the משנה and רבי do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. This is a formula for reconciling a source with an opinion

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, יום הכפורים atones even without תשובה (except for the three rebellious sins). The משנה is teaching that תשובה needs יום הכפורים to complete the atonement.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi
repentance requires Yom Kippur
Yom Kippur does not require repentance

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent contradiction raised in Step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'With תשובה' means יום הכפורים cannot work without תשובה, which goes against רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'With תשובה' means תשובה depends on יום הכפורים. That fits רבי.

steps.title: The משנה: repentance alone atones for light sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: תשובה atones for light sins, meaning an עשה and a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Repentance atones for light sins: for a positive commandment and for a negative commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can study it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה taught that מיתה and יום הכפורים need תשובה. Now it says that for light sins, תשובה works all by itself, even with no יום הכפורים. The משנה lists two kinds of light sins: failing to do an עשה, and doing a לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Repentance: regretting the sin and resolving not to repeat it
A positive commandment, something you must do
A negative commandment, something you must not do

phrases.english: Repentance atones
for light transgressions:
for a positive commandment and for a negative commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the משנה after the discussion of whether יום הכפורים needs תשובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה by itself atones for light sins: an עשה and a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Why mention the positive commandment at all?
steps.stepSummary: If תשובה atones even for a לא תעשה, which is more severe, it obviously atones for an עשה. So why does the משנה list עשה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if it atones for a negative commandment, do we even need to say it atones for a positive commandment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. It seems to say something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain לא תעשה is more severe than an עשה, because it can bring מלקות. If תשובה works for the harder case, it surely works for the easier one. So listing עשה looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it even necessary to say? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: Now, if it atones for a negative commandment,
is it necessary to say for a positive commandment?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא עַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה מְכַפֶּרֶת, עַל עֲשֵׂה מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the משנה line just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of both עשה and לא תעשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if the more severe לא תעשה is atoned, the lighter עשה obviously is, so mentioning עשה is unnecessary.

steps.title: רב יהודה: it means a prohibition fixed by a positive act
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה's 'לא תעשה' is only a לאו הניתק לעשה, a prohibition the Torah repairs with a positive action. It is about as light as an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה means: it atones for a positive commandment, and for a negative commandment that is 'transferred' to a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by reading the משנה more narrowly. The לא תעשה it means is a special, lighter kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לאו הניתק לעשה is a prohibition where the Torah gives a positive action to fix it. One example is stealing, which is fixed by returning the item. Because of that fix, there is no מלקות, so it is about as light as an עשה. Now listing עשה is not redundant, because the לא תעשה in the list is not more severe than it, and a full לא תעשה is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a reinterpretation)
A prohibition that the Torah repairs with a positive action, so there is no מלקות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב יהודה is saying this sin stops being a לא תעשה. It is still a prohibition. Its punishment is just handled differently, because the Torah gave a positive action to fix it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said,
this is what it means: for a positive commandment,
and for a negative commandment that is transferred to a positive commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by narrowing what the משנה means by לא תעשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation (הכי קאמר): narrowing the משנה's term
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's לא תעשה means any prohibition, which would make listing עשה pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's לא תעשה means only a לאו הניתק לעשה, which is no more severe than an עשה. So both are needed in the list, and a full לא תעשה is not included.

steps.title: Challenge: a baraita counts a full prohibition as light
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a full לא תעשה really cannot be atoned by תשובה alone. It begins quoting a ברייתא that lists even a לא תעשה among the light sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for a full negative commandment, does it not atone? Contrast this with a teaching: These are the light sins: a positive commandment and a negative commandment,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's narrow reading by bringing a contradicting source. It starts quoting that source, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה implied that תשובה alone does not cover a full לא תעשה. Now a ברייתא is brought that seems to call a plain לא תעשה a 'light' sin, which suggests תשובה would cover it. The rest of the ברייתא will make the contradiction complete.

keyTerms.meaning: A full, regular prohibition that is not fixed by a positive action
And contrast them: the גמרא brings a contradicting source
These are (the opening of a list)

phrases.english: And for a full negative commandment, it does not atone?
And contrast this: these are the light ones:
a positive commandment and a negative commandment,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה גָּמוּר לָא? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of רב יהודה's answer, using a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's implication that תשובה alone does not atone for a full לא תעשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא (the quote continues on the next amud) lists a plain לא תעשה among the light sins. That suggests תשובה covers even a full prohibition.
